proof:
Fix p, K, λ and an admissible lattice M as in the target, and put R=Z_(p). Use the complex basis e_i=y^i v/i! (0≤i≤λ). The divided-power formulas are X_r e_i=binom(λ-i+r,r)e_(i-r) and Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r), with out-of-range terms zero, where X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!. In particular these operators have integral matrices in this basis. Regard M_R=R⊗_Z M as a full R-lattice in V(λ), and let A_R be the image of U_Z⊗_Z R acting on V(λ). Admissibility implies A_R M_R⊆M_R.

The formulas give Y_λX_λ=E_λλ, and X_(λ-i)E_λλ=E_iλ. Also E_λλY_(λ-j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. Since λ<p, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R for every j; hence all E_λj and E_ij=E_iλE_λj belong to A_R. These are identities of complex-linear operators on V(λ), and thus preserve M_R. (For λ=0 the identity operator is the sole matrix unit and the same conclusions below apply.)

For each i define the R-submodule J_i={c∈C : c e_i∈M_R}. It is finitely generated: M_R is finitely generated over R, and E_ii M_R=J_i e_i, so J_i e_i is the image of a finitely generated module under E_ii. It is nonzero: since M_R spans V(λ) over C, E_ii M_R spans the nonzero line C e_i over C. Applying E_ij to c e_j shows J_j⊆J_i, and applying E_ji gives the reverse inclusion. Thus all J_i equal one nonzero finitely generated R-submodule J of C. For each m∈M_R, the equality m=Σ_i E_ii m shows that each of its coordinate components lies in J e_i. Conversely, each J e_i is contained in M_R by definition. Therefore M_R=⊕_(i=0)^λ J e_i. As M_R is free of rank λ+1 over the discrete valuation ring R, this decomposition shows that J is a torsion-free R-module of rank one; equivalently it is a free rank-one R-module. In particular dim_(F_p)(J/pJ)=1. The decomposition identifies M_R/pM_R, with its operators x,y,h, with the standard reduced module having basis the images of e_0,…,e_λ: choose any R-module isomorphism R≅J and use it in each summand. Localization and reduction give M_R/pM_R≅M⊗_Z F_p, and extension of scalars gives the claimed identification after tensoring with K.

Finally, on the standard reduced module, for every r≤λ<p, X_r and Y_r are scalar multiples of compositions of x and y, respectively, because r! is invertible modulo p. The matrix-unit identities above use only these divided powers and coefficients binom(λ,j), all nonzero in F_p. Thus the operators generated by x and y include every E_ij, also in characteristic 2. Any L(K)-submodule is stable under x,y and their compositions, hence under every E_ij. If it contains a nonzero vector, some coordinate c_i is nonzero; applying E_ji gives c_i e_j for each j, and scalar closure then gives every e_j. The submodule is the whole space. The module has dimension λ+1>0. This proves irreducibility for every stated M and K, including λ=0 (where it is one-dimensional).
